questions.q: How many switches are used in a 3-way switch system?
questions.n: A 3-way switch system utilizes exactly two 3-way switches to control a single fixture or load from two different locations.

questions.q: What is the common example of occupancy that uses a single-phase line?
questions.n: Standard residential dwellings typically rely on single-phase power distribution, as their typical appliance and lighting loads do not justify three-phase systems.

questions.q: What is the color of the live wire for a 3-phase line?
questions.n: In common electrical standards, including European and international conventions applied locally, black or brown represents phase/live conductors in multi-phase setups.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear depth of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: Accessibility laws specify a minimum clear depth of 1.2 meters for the elevator car to comfortably accommodate a standard wheelchair user.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: Accessibility design standards explicitly dictate a minimum interior clear car width of 1.4 meters for standard accessible compliance.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the grab bar or railings inside the elevator?
o: To act as an emergency escape mechanism anchor
To prevent passengers from touching the mirror panels
To optimize the weight distribution of the elevator car
questions.n: The explicit design intent of internal grab bars is to offer essential balance, stability, and physical support to elderly or disabled passengers during cabin acceleration and deceleration.

questions.q: What is the minimum clear width of the door of an accessible elevator?
questions.n: A minimum clear opening width of 0.9 meters is required for elevator doors to guarantee safe, unhindered passage for wheelchair users.

questions.q: What is the minimum width of a ramp landing according to accessibility standards?
questions.n: Accessibility regulations mandate that a ramp landing must have a minimum clear width of 1,200 mm to facilitate proper handling and safety.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent cap?
o: To keep debris from entering the vent system
To regulate the internal hydraulic pressure of the fixture trap
To prevent toxic sewer gases from escaping into the atmosphere
To accelerate the rate of wastewater drainage through gravity
questions.n: A vent cap is specifically engineered to shield the exposed upper terminal of a vent stack from leaves, birds, twigs, and other external debris that could clog the pipe.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a vent stack in the sanitary drainage system?
o: To channel greywater runoff directly to the municipal main storm line
To prevent grease buildup from solidifying inside the horizontal branches
To allow air to enter the drainage system and prevent siphoning
To store toxic gasses until they can be properly neutralized
questions.n: A vent stack provides vital air circulation within the plumbing network, equalizing pressures to prevent the siphoning action that could drain water seals from plumbing traps.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a cleanout?
o: To allow chemical treatments to mix thoroughly with raw blackwater
To provide access for inspection and removal of blockages
To serve as an overflow discharge point during heavy structural flooding
To filter heavy solid sediments from entering the public sewage line
questions.n: A cleanout is an accessible pipe fitting featuring a removable plug that permits direct entry for plumbing snakes or rods to inspect lines and clear structural blockages.

questions.q: What is the slope in percentage of a 100mm sewage pipe?
questions.n: Under typical plumbing and sanitation provisions, a 100mm (4-inch) pipe is permitted to have a minimum slope of 1% when space constraints require it, balancing velocity and flow depth.

questions.q: What is the common drainage slope of pipes as stated in the Plumbing Code?
questions.n: The standard baseline code requirement for horizontal drainage piping is a pitch or slope of 2% (equivalent to 1/4 inch per foot) to ensure proper scouring action.

questions.q: What is the primary purpose of a roof gutter?
o: To catch water and direct it to the downspout
To prevent thermal bridging along the roof edge structural rafters
To add an aesthetic perimeter trim to the roof eaves profile
To support the structural edge of the roof cladding or tiles
questions.n: The primary function of a roof gutter is to intercept rainwater running off the roof edge and channel it horizontally to the vertical downspouts.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a septic tank?
o: To incinerate biological solids through high thermal heat processes
To aerate blackwater through pressurized mechanical agitation pumps
To purify wastewater to standard potable drinking water quality
questions.n: A septic tank is a watertight settling chamber intended to retain and treat raw wastewater through anaerobic decomposition, separating solids from liquids before safe disposal.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a roof drain?
o: To store minor quantities of stormwater runoff to relieve stress on municipal mains
To direct water off the roof into the drainage system
To filter sediment from rainwater before storing it in a domestic cistern
To provide fresh air ventilation into the upper segments of a soil stack
questions.n: A roof drain provides a dedicated reception point on flat roof systems or valleys to capture accumulated stormwater and guide it into internal or external conductor pipes.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a downspout?
o: To relieve excessive hydraulic pressure inside internal blackwater lines
To mix stormwater with greywater for garden irrigation systems
To elevate plumbing vent lines well above the structural roof parapet
To direct rainwater from the gutter to the drainage system
questions.n: Downspouts function as vertical conductors or pipes that accept collected stormwater from horizontal roof gutters and channel it down to ground level or storm sewers.

questions.q: What do you call the cover that covers a hole in the wall for pipes?
questions.n: An escutcheon is a protective or decorative plate or ring used to cover the rough wall opening where a plumbing pipe penetrates a finished surface.

questions.q: What is used to attach pipes to the wall?
questions.n: A clamp (or pipe strap) is a structural fastening device screwed or anchored into a wall surface to support and stabilize run pipes.

questions.q: What is used to change the direction of a pipe in the plumbing system?
questions.n: An elbow is an angled pipe fitting, typically available in 45-degree or 90-degree turns, designed to change the direction of a pipe run.

questions.q: What happens when a pipe is too steep?
o: Water flows faster, which may lead to clogging
The pneumatic air balance is completely blocked, reversing the trap water seals
Hydrostatic pressure decreases, causing the pipe to collapse internally
Water flows slower, leading to increased siphonage risk
questions.n: When a pipe slope is too steep, water flows faster and separates from solid wastes, leaving the solids behind to accumulate and cause clogs.

questions.q: What is used to connect pipe flanges?
questions.n: A gasket is a flat, compressible elastomeric material placed between two mating pipe flanges to create a liquid-tight seal when bolted together.

questions.q: What connects two different sizes of pipes?
questions.n: A reducer is a specialized plumbing fitting engineered to connect a larger diameter pipe directly to a smaller diameter line.

questions.q: What is the most effective type of door to use for acoustics?
o: Double glazed glass panel with laminate
questions.n: A double-glazed glass configuration combined with a laminated interlayer provides exceptional Sound Transmission Class (STC) ratings due to the air space and vibration-damping interlayer.

questions.q: What acoustic treatment should be used on concrete to minimize vibration?
o: Perforated metal wall cladding panel panels
Acoustic plaster applied directly to the surface
questions.n: A floating floor system isolates the walking surface from the concrete structure using resilient underlayments or isolators, effectively decoupling and minimizing structural vibrations.
